summary: Well‑executed, fully preregistered paired study with complete artifact release. The experiment faithfully followed its preregistration, the analysis is deterministic and reproducible, and the reported ceiling result is transparently explained. Main weakness is that the shared_initial one‑call design and synthetic task bank produced saturation, preventing evaluation of the preregistered marginal effect; this is acceptable but requires small manuscript clarifications and additional artifact‑grounded summaries so readers can evaluate task-bank scope and validator differences.
required_revisions: Add a compact task‑taxonomy summary (counts and proportions) drawn from execution/task_manifest.jsonl showing distribution across the preregistered leaf failure classes (syntax, policy‑violation, reachability‑break, stateful‑emulation‑failure, ambiguous‑intent). Include a statement in Methods and a one‑row table in Results referencing the exact manifest path and SHA‑256.

Provide an explicit, concise description of the baseline (syntax‑only) and guarded (syntax+policy+reachability+stateful) validator logic sufficient for a reader to understand the operational difference. Cite the validator exemplar artifact path(s) and SHA‑256 (execution/scoring/*.json) and quote the exact deterministic mapping used to derive detected=1 (already archived) in one paragraph in Methods.

Add a brief artifact‑grounded summary (one paragraph and a small table or figure) of task difficulty levels (the 'difficulty.level' field from task manifests) and of whether any tasks produced nonidentical responses across the three stored response files (shared‑initial / baseline / guarded). Reference the specific execution/response SHA‑256 files (representative examples already named) and the analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and deterministic_reconciliation.json).
optional_revisions: Discuss in the Discussion a short, explicit plan (no new experiments required in this submission) for constructing a follow‑up confirmatory bank that emphasizes non‑syntactic semantic failures and multi‑draw generation per task (cite the manifest fields that would be adjusted), to guide future work.

Expand the Related Work slightly to name concrete validator systems (Batfish, Propane etc.) with precise citations if space permits; point reviewers to the manifest field that encodes policy/workflow constraints so comparisons are clearer.
